evidence: Registered qa.tester.revive@example.com; toast 'Account created successfully!' shown and user logged in as QA Tester.

actual: Registering with the same email (qa.tester.revive@example.com) a second time succeeded again, showing 'Account created successfully!' toast and returning to home page logged in, instead of being rejected.

issue: No distinct feedback for duplicate account creation
actual: Submitting registration with an already-registered email shows the same generic 'Account created successfully!' toast as a first-time registration; no error or duplicate-account warning is displayed.

evidence: Login attempt with unregistered email nonexistent.user.xyz@example.com was rejected with 'Invalid credentials. Try: emma@example.com' toast; user not logged in.

issue: Password not validated for demo/existing accounts
actual: Login page itself states 'Demo accounts... (any password works)'. Logging in as emma@example.com with an arbitrary incorrect password 'anyrandompassword' succeeded and navigated to the homepage logged in, instead of being rejected.

evidence: Submitting Create Listing form with all fields empty did not navigate/submit; browser focused the required Title field, blocking submission until required fields are filled.
Price input has min=0 constraint; entering -50 and submitting blocked the form with validationMessage 'Value must be greater than or equal to 0.' and validity=false.

Created listing 'Test Vintage Chair' with photo, description, price $150, category Furniture, condition Good, location Brooklyn NY. Toast 'Listing created successfully!' shown; product detail page displays all fields correctly.

actual: On My Listings, each item only offers 'View', 'Mark Sold', and 'Delete' actions. The product detail page for an owned listing only shows a 'Manage Your Listings' link. No Edit control or edit form exists anywhere in the DOM (verified via full-page search for 'edit' text/buttons), so sellers cannot update details like price, description, photos, or location of an existing listing.

issue: No edit/update feature for own listings
actual: Same as FT-2: only View, Mark Sold, and Delete actions are available for a seller's own listings; there is no way to modify product information after creation.

The application provides no listing-edit functionality at all (confirmed no 'Edit' controls exist in the UI or DOM), so there is no mechanism through which sellers could attempt to update another seller's product information to begin with. Since FT-2/FT-3 (update capability) fail, the constraint that depends on it cannot be demonstrated as enforced.

evidence: Typing 'Headphones' in search box filtered results to the single matching item 'Sony Noise-Canceling Headphones' ('1 items available').
Results updated immediately as text was typed into the search box, without needing to click a submit/search button.

Category filter (Furniture) narrowed 10→3 items correctly; adding Condition filter (Like New) further narrowed to 1 correct item; Sort 'Price: Low to High' correctly reordered all 10 items ascending by price ($35→$320). Price range and distance sliders also present.
Clicking category/condition filter checkboxes updated the result list and item count immediately without a submit action.
Clicked 'Add to Cart' on Sony Noise-Canceling Headphones product page; item was added (cart badge count updated to 1).
Toast notification 'Added to cart!' appeared immediately, and header cart icon updated with a badge showing '1'.

Used 'Message Seller' on a product page to send a purchase inquiry ('Hi, I'd like to purchase this item...'); toast 'Message sent to seller!' confirmed successful send. This is the app's implemented mechanism for buyers to contact sellers about purchasing.

issue: No verifiable mechanism excludes unavailable items from cart; cart state is unreliable across sessions
actual: Test: added Sofia's 'Sony Noise-Canceling Headphones' to Emma's cart (badge=1), then logged in as Sofia and marked that listing 'Sold' (toast 'Item marked as sold', browse count dropped 10→9 items, persisting across sessions). Logged back in as Emma and found the cart empty (0 items). However, a control test revealed this is NOT proof of active unavailable-item filtering: adding a still-AVAILABLE item ('Yoga Mat & Blocks Set') to Emma's cart, then logging out and back in as Emma (no ownership/availability change at all), also reset the cart to empty (no badge shown). This proves cart contents are cleared on ANY login/logout transition, regardless of item availability. Therefore the original observation is confounded and does not demonstrate a genuine 'cart cannot contain unavailable items' feature - no explicit unavailable/sold indicator, warning, or automatic-removal notice was ever observed within a cart while items were present. There is no positive evidence the app actively checks/filters cart items against current availability.

evidence: Inspected img src/alt attributes across all browse listings via DOM evaluation: each of the 9 active products has a distinct, unique Unsplash image URL (no reused/generic placeholder across items), and each image's alt text exactly matches its product title (e.g., 'Reclaimed Wood Bookshelf', 'Mid-Century Modern Armchair', 'Vintage Denim Jacket - Size M', 'Complete Harry Potter Book Set', 'Kids Wooden Train Set', etc.), consistent with the product's described category/type. No mismatched or irrelevant photos observed.
